name: Bathroom scale
description: A flat steel bathroom scale with a ribbed rubber tread and a spring dial under a small window. Stand on it to read your weight; it is too coarse for anything lighter than a person.
notes: 300 mm square and 50 mm tall: enamelled steel housing, rubber skirt and feet, tread with ribs, dial with a red needle under a glass lens at the front. Mass matches the reference. CHECK VOLUME (x2.14): the reference's 2.25 L fits a slimmer glass scale; a mechanical dial scale is about 50 mm deep. No quality: weighing in recipes means small amounts, which this cannot read.

name: Scrub brush
description: A blue plastic block with a finger ridge on top and dense rows of stiff bristles underneath, for scouring floors, pots and anything else that needs elbow grease.
notes: 140 by 60 mm and 46 mm tall: an octagonal block, a ridge to grip, a bristle bed and 44 tufts. Mass and volume match the reference. cleaning is a new quality name for hard-surface cleaning; the washing kit and the mops share it.

name: Cotton patch
description: A square of blue cotton cloth, hemmed on two sides, for patching torn clothing or straining a liquid through.
notes: 150 mm square, drawn 2 mm thick with one corner folded back; 2 mm is the finest voxel grain. CHECK VOLUME (x15.4): a single layer of cotton is a fraction of a millimetre thick, so the reference's 6 mL cannot be drawn. Mass matches the reference. The reference's sieve and strain qualities carry over as filtering, a name already in use.

name: Tattered clothes
description: A wad of old clothes too torn to wear, folded into a pile with ragged sleeves and strips hanging off. Cut up, it gives cloth for patches and rags.
notes: 250 by 200 mm and 70 mm high: a folded stack of grubby cloth with a faded shirt sleeve and a strip of denim lying over the edges. Mass matches the reference variant (1.175 kg). The reference treats it as a variant of the cotton patch, but a pile of rags looks nothing like a patch, so it has its own model as a distinct state. Volume matches the variant's 3 L.

name: Dish towel
description: A cream cotton tea towel with two red stripes, folded small with a hanging loop. Good for drying dishes, wiping surfaces or wrapping something hot.
notes: Folded to 200 by 130 mm and 16 mm thick, four layers, with stripes carried over the folded edge and a loop. CHECK VOLUME (x11.6): the reference's 43 mL is far below any folded towel; this one folds to about 0.4 L. Mass matches the reference. No quality: the reference gives none, and drying or wiping has no recipe use yet.

name: Electric hair trimmer
description: A cordless trimmer with a rubber-sided black body and a toothed steel blade on an aluminium neck. With charged batteries it cuts hair short and even.
notes: 150 mm long, 44 mm wide and 32 mm thick: tapered plastic body, rubber grip panels, sliding switch and power light on top, aluminium neck and a blade with 11 comb teeth at +x. Mass and volume match the reference. It runs on battery charge per use, as the reference does. grooming is a new quality name for hair cutting and shaving, shared with the makeshift haircut kit.

name: Hair dye kit
description: A carton holding everything for colouring hair at home: tubes of dye and developer, an applicator brush, a comb and thin plastic gloves. The front shows a face framed in rich chestnut hair.
notes: Standing carton, 150 mm wide, 210 mm tall and 70 mm deep, front on +z: white board, pink lid and band, a portrait panel and a blank label strip. Mass and volume match the reference. No quality: the reference gives none; its use is cosmetic.

name: Mop
description: A long wooden pole with a galvanised clamp and a heavy head of cotton strings. Awkward to carry, but it soaks up a spill in a few passes.
notes: 1.3 m long lying along x: 24 mm pine pole with a hanging hole, galvanised collar and wing, and a fan of 13 yarn strands over a core. Mass matches the reference. CHECK VOLUME (x9): the fanned head spreads the bounding box; the pole and strands are close to the reference's 1.5 L. cleaning 2: a mop clears spills faster than a brush or sponge.

name: Collapsible mop
description: A flat mop whose aluminium handle telescopes down to half length, with a microfibre pad on a swivel frame. Pulled out and locked, it mops a floor as well as any other.
notes: Collapsed to 600 mm: three nested aluminium sections with blue locking collars and grip, a swivel and a 350 by 120 mm pad. Mass matches the reference variant (730 g). Its own model as a distinct state: the folded handle and flat pad look nothing like the string mop. CHECK VOLUME LENGTH: the length check compares against the full string mop's 1.3 m; the pad's width spreads the bounding box, while the parts themselves are close to the variant's 760 mL.

name: Razor blade
description: A thin double-edged steel blade with a slotted centre, made to fit a safety razor. Sharp enough to cut hair, string or skin.
notes: 38 by 22 mm, drawn 2 mm thick because 2 mm is the finest voxel grain; the real blade is a tenth of a millimetre. Mirror-ground edges along both long sides and a dark slot painted flush in the middle. Mass matches the reference. cutting 1 is the same rank as other small edges.

name: Shaving kit
description: A zipped black travel case holding a razor, spare blades, a brush and a small mirror. With a bit of soap it gives a clean shave.
notes: Closed case 210 by 100 mm and 40 mm thick, plus a 14 mm carry loop: rounded nylon body, zip all round with a steel pull, a dark patch on the lid. Mass matches the reference; volume is close. Each shave uses one unit of soap, as the reference has it. grooming is the quality name, shared with the makeshift shaving kit and the hair trimmers.

name: Sponge
description: A soft yellow kitchen sponge with a green scouring pad on one side, for wiping down and scrubbing hard surfaces.
notes: 95 by 65 mm and 25 mm thick: foam with a scouring layer and a few pores on the front face. Mass and volume match the reference.

name: Makeshift haircut kit
description: A leather roll tied with cord, holding a pair of scissors, a sharpened sliver of glass and a scrap of mirror. Crude, but enough to keep hair short and out of your eyes.
notes: 200 mm long and 70 mm across: rolled leather with a lighter flap, two cord ties, bright steel scissors laid open along the top under the ties so the kit reads as a trimmer rather than a bundle, a mirror scrap against the back and a cord-wrapped glass blade out of one end. Mass and volume match the reference. grooming is shared with the electric trimmer.

name: Makeshift shaving kit
description: A small leather wallet laid open on a straight blade knapped from glass and set in a wooden grip, a shard of mirror and a nub of soap. With soap and patience it takes the stubble off.
notes: Laid open, 150 by 120 mm and 30 mm high: leather wallet with a stitched pocket and a strap, mirror shard, cord-bound wooden grip with a glass edge and a soap nub. Mass matches the reference; volume is close. Each shave uses one unit of soap, as the reference has it. grooming is shared with the travel shaving kit.

name: Washboard
description: A wooden washboard with a bed of round ribs between two stiles and a ledge at the top for the soap. Rub wet clothes up and down it with a cleaning agent to get them clean.
notes: 400 mm tall and 260 mm wide, front on +z: oak stiles and rails, birch ribs, pine backboard and a soap ledge. Mass matches the reference. CHECK VOLUME (x5): the reference's 0.9 L is a thin board; the stiles and ledge make the box 44 mm deep, though the solid wood is near 2 L. laundering is a new quality name for washing clothes; the washing kit shares it.

name: Washing kit
description: A wooden washboard with a scrub brush tied across its ribs, so the two travel together. Everything needed to scrub filthy clothing and gear clean again.
notes: 400 mm tall and 240 mm wide, front on +z: the same washboard build as the washboard, a little narrower, with a blue plastic scrub brush bound on by two cord ties. Mass matches the reference; volume is close. Carries laundering and cleaning, the qualities of its two parts.
